messages:
Jamal: Quick poll: do we want index-first as the default for remote safetensors when manifest present, or prefer stream-first with a checksum guard?
Saira: my vote is index-first for remote slow stores. avoids opening many ranges and keeps io predictable.
Nina: agree on predictability, but index-first can add latency when manifest parse is slow or gzipped. we should measure parse vs range-read cost for our S3 class
Ethan: runtime perspective: index-first helps CPU-bound parsing but hurts when we could start decode earlier via streaming. maybe hybrid: index-first for small models, stream-first for large ones
Jamal: hybrid makes sense. how do we detect small vs large? by total bytes or number of shards?
Saira: propose threshold: if total model size < 1GB -> index-first. else stream-first. make threshold config per deployment class.
Nina: add a fast-path: if manifest has a 'streamable': false flag (set during ingest for gzipped bundles), force index-first regardless of size
Ethan: good. also want to avoid duplicate IO. if two requests race to the same shard, attach to in-flight future. otherwise we double-read.
Jamal: agreed. we need attach-on-inflight in loader registry. pseudocode inlined: 
```
if registry.inflight(shard): return registry.attach_future(shard)
else: future = start_read(shard); registry.set_inflight(shard, future); return future
```
Saira: admission control idea: limit eager prefetches by concurrent_bytes_per_gpu. sample rule: max_eager_bytes = min(16GB, gpu_memory*0.2)
Nina: can we simulate patterns? i'll run a micro-sim with workloads: 1) many short seqs hitting prefix shards, 2) few long seqs streaming many layers. vary concurrency and plot p50/p99 and eager IO bytes
Ethan: add metric hooks: eager_prefetch_bytes, inflight_shard_count, attach_hit_rate. want traces to show which policy used per-request
Jamal: tests: 1) race test asserting only one physical read for two concurrent leases, 2) OOM test that triggers admission block, 3) fallback test where stream fails and index-first completes
ops-bot: (automated) created issue #2472: "warmup-defaults: hybrid index/stream heuristic + attach-on-inflight" :white_check_mark:
Saira: edge case: small shards with high dedupe (same shard used across 10 models). we should prefer keeping those resident even if eviction score decays. maybe min_residency_count threshold
Nina: add eviction_score bump: bump += log(1 + dedupe_count) when dedupe_count > 1
Ethan: when hot-swap occurs, use CAS on resident table: 
```
if resident.cas(shard, null, owner=lease): load -> resident.mark_ready()
else: attach to resident.future
```
Jamal: UX: loader API adds: prefetch_hint: "mode": "hybrid", "maybe_stream_threshold_bytes": 1073741824, "lease_id": "..."
Saira: also add hint: "expected_resident_bytes" so admission controller can budget before IO finishes
Nina: sim tasks: i'll include probabilistic lease durations and cancel rates to tune TTLs and cancellation heuristics
Ethan: one more: fallback order should be runtime-configurable per namespace: e.g., ["zero-copy","stream","index"] or ["stream","index","mmap"]
Jamal: ok. next steps: Nina -> sim and perf matrix, Saira -> PR for loader API schema + admission config, Ethan -> implement attach-on-inflight & CAS handoff, Jamal -> write test cases and add to CI smoke.
ops-bot: (automated) linked PR 712 added to issue #2472
Jamal: thanks all. will summarize changes in the RFC follow-up doc and link here. if anyone wants different default thresholds, speak up before PRs land :thumbsup:
